hero.title: Study Information Technology in France for Indian Students
hero.subtitle: Advance your enterprise technology career in France at prestigious Grandes Écoles and research universities, benefiting from Europe's booming cloud and cybersecurity initiatives. Indian students gain specialized IT training, affordable tuition, and up to 2 years of post-study stay-back under the Franco-Indian partnership.

overview: France is driving major European technological sovereignty initiatives in cloud infrastructure, telecommunications, and digital security. Studying Information Technology in France offers Indian students high-caliber technical instruction across enterprise network management, cloud architectures, and operational cyber defense, enriched by Europe's thriving startup and corporate technology sectors.

French public universities and specialized engineering institutions offer English-taught 3-year Bachelor's and 2-year Master of Science in Information Technology (MSc IT) programs. Academic curricula emphasize enterprise database management, distributed cloud platforms, network protocol engineering, IT governance, and cybersecurity operations, with students benefiting from subsidized public tuition and mandatory corporate internship semesters.

Upon completing a recognized Master's degree in France, Indian students can access post-study work authorization under the Carte de Séjour Recherche d'Emploi ou Création d'Entreprise (RECE). Supported by the Franco-Indian bilateral partnership on student mobility, Indian Master's alumni are eligible for up to a 2-year post-study stay-back period, providing ample time to launch careers as Cloud Engineers, Systems Specialists, and Network Administrators in Paris, Lyon, or Toulouse.

sections.title: Why study Information Technology in France?
sections.lead: Information Technology (IT) in France for Indian Students IT studies in France are a great option for international students to learn technical skills in a country with a solid higher-education system and a diverse technology sector. Students can choose to specialize in areas like software development, cybersecurity, cloud computing, data science, artificial intelligence, networking and information systems.

items: In France, IT-related courses are offered by public universities, engineering schools and private institutions. Depending on the university and course, students may study in French, in English, or in both.
The major advantages of studying Information Technology in France are:
Access to undergraduate, graduate, and specialized computing programs.
Opportunities to specialize in security, cloud infrastructure, software engineering and data analytics.
Many programs include practical projects, research opportunities and internships.
Access to European technology companies and international research networks.
Possible career opportunities in France and other international job markets.
Students can find these opportunities and know the requirements involved in studying abroad through Edu Hawk worldwide study abroad guidance.

sections.title: Courses in Information Technology in France
sections.lead: In France, Information Technology programs are offered under a number of related course titles, such as Computer Science, Informatics, Information Systems, Software Engineering, and Network Engineering.

items: Popular IT Disciplines
Software Engineering: Design, programming, testing and application development of software.
Cyber Security: Network security, information security, cryptography and risk management.
Cloud Computing: Managing infrastructure, virtualization, distributed systems, cloud platforms.
AI and Data Science: Data analysis, intelligent systems, machine learning.
Networking and Systems Administration: Operating systems, system maintenance, network architecture.
Information Systems Management: Business technology, databases, enterprise systems, and digital transformation.
High Performance Computing: Parallel, distributed and large scale computing.
Course Duration

rows: Typically 5 years of post-secondary education, depending on the path
Varies depending on qualification and institution

items: A Master's in Information Technology in France or similar typically requires 120 ECTS credits over two years. Students should check the institution's website for the exact program structure, language of instruction and entry requirements.

sections.title: Eligibility for Admission
sections.lead: To get onto a postgraduate IT or computer science program, international students usually need a relevant undergraduate degree.

items: The specific requirements vary depending on the university and the selected specialization.
A bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering or a closely related discipline.
Good academic results in previous studies.
Understanding of programming, algorithms, mathematics and computing basics relevant to the course.
Fluency in English for English-language programs or French for French-language programs.
Relevant projects, internships, or work experience as applicable or as recommended.
Some specialized programs will accept students from a mathematics, electronics or related engineering background, provided they have the necessary computing knowledge.
Admission is not assured by fulfilling the minimal requirements. Universities look at the whole application, academic preparation and suitability for the course of choice.

sections.title: Admission Requirements for IT in France
sections.lead: Universities can have different entrance requirements for their master's degrees. Applicants are advised to read the program specific page before applying.

items: Applicants are normally expected to have a recognized Bachelor's degree and academic transcripts to demonstrate adequate preparation for advanced studies in computing. Some programs may require prior study of programming, data structures, algorithms, operating systems, databases, or mathematics.

For English-taught programs, universities may require an accepted English-language test or other evidence of proficiency. The test you'll need to take and the minimum score you must achieve depends on the program. Some institutions may accept prior English-medium education on a case by case basis.
French Language Requirement

You may be asked to prove your proficiency in French by taking a recognized language test or obtaining a certificate for programs taught in French. Students should check the language level required by the university and the documents accepted.
Additional Selection Criteria
Some courses might include:
Statement of Purpose (SOP) or motivation letter
References.
Build a technical portfolio or projects.
Relevant work experience.
Interview or further assessment.

sections.title: Cost of studying Information Technology in France
sections.lead: The cost of studying Information Technology in France depends on the university, program, city, nationality and tuition exemption eligibility.

items: Tuition Fees for 2026-2027
The annual registration fee refers to the applicable fees for public higher-education institutions under the national fee system:
Bachelor's Degree (Licence) | €178 | €2,902
Master's Degree | €255 | €3,950
Doctorate | €398 | €398

These are national public institution rates, not universal prices for every IT program. Some institutions or courses may charge different fees and exemptions may be granted depending on the student's status or the institution's rules. Private institutions and specialized programs can cost considerably more.
Other Costs
Students should also make provisions for:
Lodging and utilities.
Food and the price of everyday living.
Public transportation.
Applicable insurance and health-related costs.
Books, equipment and personal expenses.
Visa related costs and the Student and Campus Life Contribution (CVEC), where applicable.
Cost of living varies a lot from city to city. Accommodation in Paris is generally more expensive than in many other French university cities. Base the budget on the city not on tuition fees.
International students should look into French government scholarships, university scholarships, exchange programs and other funding opportunities.
Schemes differ in terms of eligibility, award amounts and deadlines.

sections.title: Process of Admission to Information Technology in France
sections.lead: The admission process for IT courses in France varies depending on the degree level, nationality, institution and program.

items: Choose a Programme: Identify IT-related master's programs that match your academic profile and chosen specialization.
Check Eligibility: Review the degree requirements, language requirements, and application deadlines.
Collect Your Documents: This includes transcripts, degree certificates, CV, Statement of Purpose, and language-test results, where required.
Apply on the Right Platform: Follow the university's application instructions. Depending on your situation, the route can be via the university's own portal.
Full Selection Process: You will be asked to supply additional documentation, attend an interview or undertake an assessment if necessary.
Get and look at the offer: Check out the program, fees, conditions and enrollment deadlines.
Arrange Your Student Visa: If you have to, follow instructions from official sources for your nationality and circumstances.
Complete Enrolment: Provide all required original or verified documents and pay any applicable fees.
Application dates differ per institution. Start preparing early, especially if you need document translation, language testing or visa processing.

sections.title: Recognition and Accreditation
sections.lead: Students are advised to confirm the exact status of the qualification prior to enrollment. In France, a nationally recognized master's degree is not the same as a university diploma or a certificate issued by a private institution.

items: Applicants need to check:
The type of qualification awarded by the program (i.e. national master's degree or other).
Whether the program and institution are officially recognized.
Level of qualification and ECTS credits.
Whether the degree satisfies the requirements of employers or professional bodies in the country where you intend to work.
Whether any necessary professional recognition applies to their chosen career.

The marketing name of a program does not in itself determine its recognition status. Award confirmation Students should consult the institution's official program description and appropriate sources of higher-education information in France.

sections.title: Salary and Job Opportunities after Studying
sections.lead: A French Information Technology qualification can lead to careers in technology, finance, telecommunications, consulting, health care, manufacturing, retail and public services. Job prospects are dependent on technical ability, experience, language skills and location and employer requirements.

items: Jobs & Careers
Graduates can pursue roles such as:
Software Developer / Software Engineer
System Administrator / IT Support Specialist.
Network Engineering.
Cyber security analyst.
Cloud / Infrastructure Engineer.
Database admin.
Junior Data Engineer or Data Analyst.
IT Project Coordinator or Business Analyst.
Engineer, Systems.
Research or Development Engineer depending on specialization.
Expected salary

There is no unique salary for IT graduates in France. Pay varies with the role, region, employer, experience and technical specialization. Entry-level jobs tend to pay less than those for experienced engineers or specialists. Salaries for cybersecurity, cloud computing, software development, and data jobs can vary according to the particular skills required.
Job Opportunities
Develop a portfolio of projects and practical technical skills.
Seek out internships or work-study opportunities if they are available.
Develop professional French, particularly for positions with local clients or teams.
Learn tools and technologies relevant to the job you're targeting.
Utilize university career services and professional networking opportunities.
Verify work authorization and post-study residence rules from official French government sources.

faqs.q: Is France a good place to study Information Technology?
faqs.a: In France there are many public universities and specialized institutes providing courses related to computer science, software development, cyber security, networks and data. The best fit will depend on the course content, the teaching language, the fees and your career goals.

faqs.q: What's the cost of a master's in IT in France?
faqs.a: The regular registration fee for a master's degree at a public university for the academic year 2026–2027, according to the fee information, is €255 per year for students from the EU/EEA/Switzerland and €3,950 for non-EU students with differentiated fees.

faqs.q: What bachelor's degree is required for an IT master's in France?
faqs.a: A degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering or a related field is usually acceptable. Some programs also accept other quantitative or engineering backgrounds, provided that the applicant possesses sufficient computing knowledge.

faqs.q: What jobs can I do after an IT master's degree in France?
faqs.a: The possible job titles are Software Engineer, Systems Administrator, Network Engineer, Cybersecurity Analyst, Cloud Engineer, Data Analyst, and IT Project Coordinator. The employment outcome depends on the specialization chosen, practical experience, language ability and work authorization.
